key_insight: OpenFrontiers separates mathematical rediscovery from solution retrieval, finding that closed-book LLM agents rarely solve recently resolved research problems.
engineering_relevance: Lean 4 statements, isolated proof checking, and controlled retrieval conditions offer a framework for evaluating research-level reasoning beyond answer matching.
method: Compile a structured corpus of 12,151 open research problems.
Build a 200-problem mathematics benchmark with Lean 4 statements checked by automated probes and two independent reviews.
Evaluate seven LLM agents on HQ-50 under standardized budgets and closed-book, frozen-retrieval, and live-web conditions.
evidence_signal: On HQ-50, closed-book agents solved at most 7 of 40 resolved problems, while live-web success mostly reflected retrieval of published solutions.
watch_item: Access to published solutions can confound rediscovery claims, so retrieval conditions must be reported explicitly.
paper_title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
